original_query: select c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice, sum(l_quantity) from customer, orders, lineitem where o_orderkey in ( select l_orderkey from lineitem group by l_orderkey having sum(l_quantity) > 313 ) and c_custkey = o_custkey and o_orderkey = l_orderkey group by c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice order by o_totalprice desc, o_orderdate limit 100;
rewritten_query:
WITH order_sums AS (
    SELECT l_orderkey,
           SUM(l_quantity) AS sum_quantity
    FROM lineitem
    GROUP BY l_orderkey
    HAVING SUM(l_quantity) > 313
)
SELECT c.c_name,
       c.c_custkey,
       o.o_orderkey,
       o.o_orderdate,
       o.o_totalprice,
       os.sum_quantity
FROM order_sums os
JOIN orders o ON o.o_orderkey = os.l_orderkey
JOIN customer c ON c.c_custkey = o.o_custkey
ORDER BY o.o_totalprice DESC, o.o_orderdate
LIMIT 100;

rewrite_suggestion.produced_suggestion: Replace the IN subquery with a join to a pre-aggregated derived table (CTE), which avoids the semi-join and reuses the aggregation result.

The original scans lineitem twice (once for the IN subquery, once for the outer join) and recomputes SUM(l_quantity) via the outer GROUP BY. Pre-aggregating lineitem once scans the 60M-row table only once and eliminates the final GroupAggregate.

The redundant outer GROUP BY on c_name, c_custkey, o_orderkey, o_orderdate, o_totalprice is removed: after pre-aggregation, one row per qualifying order exists, and o_orderkey/c_custkey uniqueness guarantees no duplicate rows.

Converted implicit comma joins into explicit JOINs; the join order starts from the small filtered aggregated set (~133K qualifying orders) and joins to orders by primary key and customer by primary key.
The HAVING threshold > 313 is retained as a literal; no additional foldable constants are present.
